powdercoating.title: Powder Coating
powdercoating.cardTeaser: A dry-powder finish baked on, not brushed on — harder, thicker, and built to outlast paint.
powdercoating.oneliner: A dry-powder finish baked on, not brushed on — harder, thicker, and built to outlast paint.
powdercoating.explanation: Powder coating applies a dry polymer powder to the steel using an electrostatic charge, then cures it in an oven until it melts into a smooth, continuous shell. Because there's no solvent flashing off as it dries, the coating goes on more evenly and comes out considerably tougher than liquid paint — better resistance to chipping, scratching, and fading from sun exposure. It's the finish behind the flat, factory-grade color you see on our table frames, chair bases, and gates, and it holds up to daily handling far better than a brushed-on topcoat.
powdercoating.turnaround: Turnaround depends on piece size, color, and order volume — confirmed for your project when you request a quotation.

process.step1: Clean and pre-treat the metal so the powder has a bare, contaminant-free surface to bond to
process.step2: Mask off any threads, hinges, or fittings that need to stay bare metal
process.step3: Apply the powder electrostatically, coating every edge and corner evenly, then cure in the oven until it flows into a continuous film
process.step4: Cool, inspect for coverage, and touch up any thin spots before it ships

welding.title: Welding
welding.cardTeaser: Fusing steel into a single structural piece — the joinery behind every frame, base, and gate we build.
welding.oneliner: Fusing steel into a single structural piece — the joinery behind every frame, base, and gate we build.
welding.explanation: Welding is how separate cuts of steel become one solid structure: heat melts the metal at the joint and it fuses as it cools, producing a bond as strong as the base material itself. This is the step that turns flat laser-cut panels and bar stock into an X-base table, a chair frame, or a gate — anywhere strength and rigidity matter more than a mechanical fastener would allow. Clean, well-ground welds also matter for looks, not just strength, since a visible seam on furniture or a gate reads as unfinished.
welding.methods: Suited to structural steel joins across frames, bases, and gates — mitered corners, flush seams, and hidden joints, ground smooth for a finished look.
welding.turnaround: Turnaround depends on the complexity of the assembly — confirmed for your project when you request a quotation.

process.step1: Cut and prep each piece to size, with edges squared for a clean fit
process.step2: Fit up and clamp the pieces in position, checking alignment and angles, then tack weld to hold it in place
process.step3: Run the final weld pass along every joint that needs full strength
process.step4: Grind and smooth the welds so seams disappear, then check the frame for square, level, and structural soundness

lasercutting.title: Laser Cutting
lasercutting.cardTeaser: CNC-precise cuts in steel sheet — the detail work behind our Greek-key trim and pattern gates.
lasercutting.oneliner: CNC-precise cuts in steel sheet — the detail work behind our Greek-key trim and pattern gates.
lasercutting.explanation: A CNC laser traces a design file through steel sheet with a level of precision and repeatability a hand tool can't match, which is what makes intricate, repeating patterns — like the Greek-key trim and vertical-slat work you'll see on our gates — possible at all. It also means every piece in a run comes out identical, so hardware, brackets, and decorative panels line up and fit the way they're designed to. It's the right process anytime a project calls for a custom pattern, tight tolerances, or clean edges that need no reworking before they're welded or finished.
lasercutting.precision: Cuts hold tight, repeatable tolerances sheet after sheet, so patterned pieces and hardware line up without hand-fitting.
lasercutting.turnaround: Turnaround depends on pattern complexity and sheet thickness — confirmed for your project when you request a quotation.

process.step1: Prepare the cut file from the approved design or pattern, and load the steel sheet at the required thickness
process.step2: Run the laser cut, tracing every line and detail from the file
process.step3: Deburr the cut edges so they're smooth to the touch
process.step4: Dry-fit pieces against the design to confirm patterns and hardware line up, then hand off to welding or finishing

sandblasting.title: Sandblasting
sandblasting.cardTeaser: Abrasive-blasted prep that strips steel back to bare metal so finishes actually stick.
sandblasting.oneliner: Abrasive-blasted prep that strips steel back to bare metal so finishes actually stick.
sandblasting.explanation: Sandblasting drives abrasive media at high pressure against the steel surface to strip away rust, mill scale, and old coatings down to bare metal, while leaving a slightly roughened texture (a 'profile') that gives the next coating something to grip. Skipping this step is the most common reason a powder coat or paint job fails early — flaking or bubbling because it was applied over a surface that was contaminated or too smooth to bond to. We use it both as prep before finishing and as a standalone service for anyone restoring old steel that needs to be brought back to clean metal.
sandblasting.turnaround: Turnaround depends on surface area and condition — confirmed for your project when you request a quotation.

process.step1: Inspect the surface for rust, scale, or existing coatings, and mask off any areas that need to stay untouched
process.step2: Blast the surface with abrasive media until it's clean, bare metal
process.step3: Clear away dust and blast residue from every edge and cavity, then inspect the surface profile
process.step4: Move straight to priming or powder coating to prevent flash rust from setting in
